paragraphs: Here's what Psalm 88 teaches, friend: you can pray without a happy ending. Heman never gets one in this psalm. His last words are "darkness is my closest companion." (Psalm 88:18) And God put that prayer in His Word anyway, which tells me honest pain is welcome in His house.

Look at what Heman does in the middle of all that dark. He says, "day and night I cry out before You." (Psalm 88:1) He asks hard questions, and then he says, "But to You, O LORD, I cry for help." (Psalm 88:13) Every complaint in this psalm gets aimed straight at the LORD, the God of his salvation. I think that's the whole lesson, friend: when it's dark, you can take it to Him.

So if you've got a night with no bright ending, don't feel like you have to dress it up before you pray. I sat in the back of a dark junk drawer for years, so I know that dark can feel long. You can bring the whole heavy thing to the LORD, just like Heman did. Come as you are, and keep showing up, because the One who hears you is the One who saves.
